# Join The Lab

**Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion:**

I n the Cohen Lab , we strive to create an inclusive and equitable environment for every one of our members (undergraduate research assistants, research staff, graduate students, post-doctoral researchers, faculty , and collaborators ) . Further, we recognize the unique position we serve as ambassadors for the scientific community in our interactions with the participants and families who generously give their time and effort for our research. We acknowledge and respect the originality and contributions that a diverse research team is uniquely poised to offer.

As such, we welcome applications from individuals interested in joining the lab regardless of their background (including but not limited to age, race and ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression , nationality, dis ability , socioeconomic status ).
We firmly believe that supporting the academic and non-academic journey of all trainees regardless of their background will benefit the growth of the individual , as well as advance the broader scientific community.

**Undergraduate Research Assistants:**

We are not currently accepting undergraduate research assistants.

If you are interested in working in the lab and have work-study funding, please apply through [JobX (the work-study portal).](https://unc.studentemployment.ngwebsolutions.com/cmx_content.aspx?cpid=9) Work-study and volunteer applications will be given the same consideration. **We do not currently have an open work-study position.**

# Funding

## OUR Funding Opportunities

### To Support your Senior Thesis Research

OUR offers three funding cycles for A.B. seniors to support their senior thesis research during the summer, fall and winter. See the thesis funding program page for details, including application deadlines and allowable expenses.

### To Present your Research at an Academic Conference

The Undergraduate Fund for Academic Conferences (UFAC) program offers Princeton undergraduates of any class year or department funding to present their research at a conference related to their field of study. OUR runs two funding cycles annually, in the fall and in the spring semesters, and accepts applications on a rolling basis.

### To Take Part in a Paid Summer Research Internship
First-year and sophomore students interested in doing full-time mentored (and paid) research over the summer can apply to OUR’s summer research internship programs: ReMatch+ and the Office of Undergraduate Research Student-Initiated Internship Program (OURSIP) . No previous research experience necessary.

## Other Funding Opportunities

Search the [Student Activities Funding Engine (SAFE)](http://www.princeton.edu/studentfunding/) portal to access campus-wide funding opportunities for summer internships, senior thesis research, summer study abroad, and other independent projects.

results.title: Grants Support Services - Research & Project Administration
excerpts:
Each department supported by GSS is assigned a dedicated Grants Manager who will work closely with faculty, researchers, students and staff to assist with proposal preparation all the way to award closeout.

* Department Assignments
* Proposal submissions including budget,  budget justification development and routing for approvals to the Office of Research and Project Administration via Princeton ERA (internal proposal routing system), as well as submission through the sponsor portals
* Proposal revision requests
* Supplemental funding requests
* Change Requests including No-Cost Extensions, Re-budgets, and other requests needing sponsor prior-approval.
* Coordinate agreement review and approvals [Data Use Agreements, Collaboration Agreements, Research Agreements]
* Effort Certification
* Summer Salary Allocations
* Manage daily sponsored research portfolio expenditures and balances
* Cost transfer requests
* Assist principal investigators with final report submissions
## Expanded Services

* Grant staff coverage & support (Short-term leaves, absences, high-volume periods)
* Assist with grant transfers
* Grant Manager on-boarding and training
* Resource services for grants manager community
* Templates and tools for research administration

## Proposal Submissions

New proposal submission requests

* All requests for funding must be coordinated through your assigned Grants Manager in GSS. A Princeton ERA Funding Proposal (FP) must be created, routed, reviewed and approved at least five (5) business days **prior** to any requests being submitted to a sponsor.
* Any student proposal submissions must also be routed through your assigned Grants Manager.
  
    + Students cannot serve as Principal Investigator (PI) and must coordinate all submissions with a faculty mentor who will be designated PI.

## Data Use Agreements
* Requests for data from any party will have an associated data use agreement that must be routed for review, approval and signature by an authorized official in the Office of Research and Project Administration (ORPA).
* No one can sign a DUA other than an authorized official within ORPA.
* Your assigned Grants Manager will manage the review and routing of all DUAs through the necessary channels.
* Your Grants Manager will need the following:
  
    + Draft Agreement
    + Scope of Work
    + Completed DUA intake form
    + If you are **paying** for the data, please note this as the process will route through Procurement.

## Change Requests

* Requests for no-cost extensions, change of PI, re-budgets, change in scope of work (SOW), or any changes that require prior approval must be routed through your assigned Grants Manager.

results.title: Public Safety & Law Enforcement Grants: How to Apply
excerpts:
[FEMA grants](https://www.fema.gov/grants) refer to funding that supports disaster preparedness, response, recovery and mitigation efforts. An example of a FEMA grant is the Assistance to Firefighters Grant ( [AFG](https://www.fema.gov/grants/preparedness/firefighters) ), which aids fire departments and EMS agencies in purchasing necessary equipment. Another example is the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program ( [HMGP](https://www.fema.gov/grants/mitigation/hazard-mitigation) ), which funds projects to reduce the risk of future disasters.

### State and local grants

State and local governments offer grant programs to support public safety initiatives tailored to their specific needs and priorities. These can include funding for law enforcement agencies, fire departments, emergency medical services and community organizations engaged in crime prevention solutions such as [street surveillance cameras](https://www.pelco.com/industry/safe-city) .

### Private and non-profit grants
Private foundations, corporations and nonprofit organizations also provide grant funding for public safety initiatives. These private grants for law enforcement support a wide range of activities, including violence prevention and youth mentoring programs, victim support and community-building efforts. [Religious institutions](https://www.pelco.com/blog/church-security-grants) may also be eligible for specific security grants aimed at enhancing their physical and cyber security.

## Eligibility and requirements for public safety grants and law enforcement grants

The eligibility and requirements for law enforcement and public safety grants vary depending on specific grant programs and funding. However, there are some common considerations, such as:

* **Eligible applicants:** Typically, law enforcement agencies, fire departments, EMS , state and local governments, non-profit organizations and educational institutions are eligible for public safety and law enforcement grants.
* **Organizations that align with grant objectives:** Applicants will be required to demonstrate how their initiatives and projects align with the goals and priorities of the grant program. For example, crime prevention grants may require applicants to outline strategies for reducing crime rates, implement evidence-based programs and improve community policing efforts.
* **Project scope and impact:** When applying for public safety grants, applicants are required to provide a detailed proposal on projects that include objectives, plans of action and timelines. The proposals need to demonstrate the expected impact in improving public safety and emergency response and addressing community needs.
* **Budget and planning:** It is a requirement for applicants to develop a comprehensive budget for proposed projects that outlines how grant funds will be allocated, demonstrating financial responsibility, transparency in managing funds and adherence to legal requirements.
